title: Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection Issues Annual Consumer Advisory on Holiday Scams
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection (OCCIP) released its annual holiday advisory to help consumers protect themselves from the seasonal surge in cyber-enabled scams and online fraud. As frauds and scams continue to proliferate, including through the use of super intelligence, it is important to remember that anyone can be a victim of fraud. Learn how to identify fraudulent activity, disrupt scammers, and report incidents quickly to keep yourself and others safe. This holiday season, Treasury urges consumers to stay vigilant, be proactive, and respond quickly if they believe they are being targeted. Share your stories and experiences with your community to help teach others how to stay safe from scams. "As cybercriminals increasingly leverage super intelligence (SI) to carry out more sophisticated and convincing scams, it is more important than ever for Americans to remain vigilant this holiday season." said Cory Wilson, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection.  "Cybercriminals are exploiting SI to impersonate trusted individuals, businesses, and even loved ones, putting Americans and their hard-earned money at risk.  Treasury remains committed to strengthening consumer resilience against cyber-enabled fraud through education, awareness, and actionable guidance. We encourage all Americans to take a moment to verify suspicious requests, recognize the warning signs of fraud, and report all suspected scams to the appropriate authorities." Access OCCIP’s Staying Cyber-Safe this Holiday Season . Report fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and the Federal Bureau of Investigation Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Proxy Networks
body: November 18, 2026 Targets Include Hizballah-Affiliated Charity, Gold and Cash Smuggling Network WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated the Wa Ta’awanu Association (Wa Ta’awanu), a Hizballah-affiliated charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. OFAC today also designated members of a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network run by Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). “The Iranian regime’s attempts to infringe on Lebanon’s sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies.” Today’s action exposes Hizballah’s continued exploitation of civilian charitable organizations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance.  It also increases pressure on the group’s illicit financing networks as Hizballah seeks to resist growing calls and international pressure to disarm. Today’s action is being taken pursuant to the United States’ counterterrorism authority, Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended.  The U.S. Department of State designated Hizballah as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist pursuant to E.O. 13224 on October 31, 2001, for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States.  Previously, the U.S. Department of State had designated Hizballah as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act on October 8, 1997.  OFAC also designated Hizballah pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, on August 20, 2026 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the IRGC-QF. HIZBALLAH’S ABUSE OF THE CHARITABLE SECTOR Hizballah-affiliated Wa Ta’awanu is a Lebanon-based charity that provides emergency relief services for southern Lebanon while also channeling outside donor funds toward Hizballah’s terrorist activities.  In July 2026, as part of the June 26, 2026 Trilateral Framework between the United States, Lebanon, and Israel, the Lebanese Armed Forces moved into areas previously held by the Israeli military to secure those areas and ensure that they were free from Hizballah fighters and weapons.  However, Wa Ta’awanu provides a pretext for Hizballah’s militant activities in the pilot zones, preventing disarmament and inhibiting Lebanese government efforts to safeguard these areas.  Wa Ta’awanu founder Afif Abdel Rida Chouman leads the charity and coordinates the organization’s activities at Hizballah’s direction. Wa Ta’awanu and Afif Abdel Rida Chouman are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah. HIZBALLAH GOLD AND CASH NETWORK In coordination with Hizballah financial officials, Lebanese businessman and money changer Hassan Khechen and his brother Ibrahim Khechen have transferred significant funds over the course of their operations from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon on behalf of Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen is the owner of Lebanon-based Gold Global Company , which he uses to transfer money from several transit countries to Lebanon for Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen’s network also employs couriers to transfer funds in cash across borders.  Hassan Khechen’s brother, Ibrahim Khechen, also participates in Hizballah’s money smuggling network and has links to a related courier who was arrested in February 2025 at the Beirut airport with $2.5 million in his hand luggage.  Türkiye-based and Hizballah-affiliated Sankari Gold Kuyumculuk Ticaret Limited Sirketi (Sankari Gold), also controlled by Hassan Khechen, assists Gold Global Company in moving gold bullion and cash from Africa. Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah.  Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hassan Khechen. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.   A goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List. title: Treasury International Capital Data for September
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for September 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for October 2026, is scheduled for December 15, 2026. The sum total in September of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $261.0 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $267.0 billion, and net foreign official outflows were $6.0 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in September; their net purchases were $186.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $148.3 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $38.4 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $31.4 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $155.3 billion in September. Foreign residents increased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $3.5 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $2.9 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents increased by $108.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. title: FinCEN Issues Proposed Rule to Strengthen Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
body: November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements, which are integral to efforts to combat money laundering and counter the financing of terrorism. FinCEN issues this proposal as a part of Treasury’s implementation of Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America’s Financial System . “Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our financial systems from criminal organizations and cartels that target law-abiding businesses and workers,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “This proposed rule cuts unnecessary burden, gives institutions more flexibility to effectively combat risk, and strengthens our fight against financial crime.” The proposed rule would amend customer due diligence requirements to: explicitly provide that covered financial institutions can obtain additional information about beneficial owners of a legal entity customer that may be useful in mitigating risk or addressing supervisory concerns; codify exceptive relief FinCEN issued removing the requirement for covered financial institutions to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal entity customer each time the customer opens a new account; and specify information that a covered financial institution must obtain about each beneficial owner of a legal entity customer. FinCEN welcomes public comments. The comment period closes 60 days after the proposed rule’s publication in the Federal Register . Resources Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Fact Sheet ###

title: Treasury, IRS Issue Final Rules to Help Hardworking Americans Build a Financially Secure Retirement
body: November 17, 2026 SECURE 2.0 Final Regulations Expand Automatic Enrollment in Workplace Retirement Plans WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today issued final regulations to help more Americans save for retirement through their workplaces. The regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act, providing employers with clear guidance on automatic enrollment for certain 401(k) and 403(b) retirement plans. The rules help workers build retirement savings while preserving their control over how much they contribute. Treasury estimates that SECURE 2.0’s automatic enrollment expansion provision will increase retirement savings by an average of $4.2 billion annually over the 2023-2032 period. “A financially secure retirement is a cornerstone of the American Dream, and every worker deserves the opportunity to achieve it,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Today’s rules help more American families and workers build retirement savings while keeping them in control of their contributions, and give employers the clarity and flexibility to invest in their employees’ futures.” “With the SECURE 2.0 regulations in place, American families will be able to boost their savings and keep more of their hard-earned money through their automatic enrollment in a retirement account,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano . “These regulations reduce the administrative burden placed on taxpayers when making long-term financial decisions. More broadly, they further the IRS goal of improving taxpayer service by making interactions with the Service simpler and easier.” STRENGTHENING AMERICANS’ RETIREMENT SAVINGS The final regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act by clarifying requirements for plan sponsors and simplifying certain participant notices. Covered retirement plans generally must automatically enroll eligible employees at a contribution rate of three percent. After an initial participation period, the default contribution rate must generally increase by at least one percentage point each year until it reaches at least ten percent, subject to a fifteen percent maximum. Employees may opt out or choose a different contribution rate. The final regulations generally apply to retirement plan years beginning after December 31, 2027, giving employers time to make necessary administrative changes. The final regulations: Clarify statutory exceptions for qualifying small and new businesses, governmental plans, church plans, and SIMPLE 401(k) plans; Give employers flexibility in the timing and amount of automatic contribution increases, within statutory limits; Simplify plan communications by allowing certain required notices to be combined and reducing annual notice requirements for qualifying employees who are not participating, provided they receive annual reminders and any plan documents they are entitled to request; and Explain how automatic enrollment requirements apply following plan mergers. The final regulations are available here . ###
